claims.title: Gaussian ensemble migration with preserved evaluated response records

quoted_fields.interface: Archived X_1:M iidN(p,sigma^2 I_d),unknown fixed EXOGENOUS p;current independent sourceQ=N(q,sigma^2 I_d),unknown fixed EXOGENOUS q;known common covariance and independent acquisition windows. Historical source is UNAVAILABLE;only these records/functions are retained. Responses are a FIXED deterministicF or independent stochastic kernelH(x,.),including solver configuration,relevant initial state andfailure treatment. Consumer needs an ANONYMOUS distribution-level ensemble withfull joint law product_i Q(dy_i)H(y_i,dell_i),not responses to the particular factual current readingsW_i. Coupling decisions must not inspect response values. New ensemble is iid internally,not independent of the old version.
quoted_fields.failure: Gaussian family,common covariance,independent acquisition and fixed exogenous means are supplied model premises,not certified by a finite normality test. Extra historical records,known means/densities,replayable seeds or current factual-input requirements change the interface. Exact known conditional Gaussian probabilities are legitimately used;unknown density estimates are not treated as exact. Affine Gaussian transport has the same information and correct iid law but changes every input;it can win with cheap exact response updates. Known-density maximal coupling/importance mixing,importance weighting for weaker expectation outputs,shared seeds andbest incremental solvers remain legitimate comparators when their access/output contracts hold. No first-recycling-method or priority claim. Finite-grid law is approximate;continuous minimax theorem does not prove finite-grid optimality. Repeated grid migrations accumulate approximation error. No expected bit-complexity or fixed-latency theorem;resolution must already exist in historical records. Gaussian-model/covariance/clipping error needs extra allowances.
